topic.label: Claude Tag
topic.desc: Claude Tag: Overview (Claude Tag), Concepts, Admins, Users.

concepts: Overview (Claude Tag): Work with Claude Tag.

Concepts: How Claude Tag works, Glossary, How agent identity works, Personal connectors in channels, Security and data handling, Data lifecycle and deletion, Claude Tag settings map, Claude Tag for Claude Code users.

Admins: What the Claude Slack app can access, Set up Claude Tag, Give Claude access to your tools, Configure GitHub access, Configure GitLab access, Set a spend limit, Set up Claude Tag for on-call, Per-service connection guides, Connect a service that isn't in the list, Connect Amplitude, Connect Asana, Connect Jira and Confluence and 34 more.

Users: Get started, Commands Claude Tag understands, Control when Claude Tag responds, Use Claude Tag in a group DM, Good habits for working with Claude Tag, Set up routines, What Claude Tag remembers, Choose the model Claude Tag uses, Prompt library, Troubleshoot Claude Tag in channels and DMs, Use case library, Triage requests and 12 more.
skills: Claude Tag puts Claude in your Slack channels with admin-governed access. See what to hand it, how setup works, and where to start as an admin or end user.
Each Claude Tag thread in Slack runs a working session in a sandbox. See how progress shows in the thread, how to steer mid-task, what survives between turns, and how memory is scoped.
Claude Tag terms defined in one place, including agent identity, bundle, connector, personal connector, scope, Agent Proxy, routine, and session.

Claude Tag acts under its own service accounts in Slack channels, not as you. See how channel access is bounded, how credentials reach it, how Claude uses your personal connectors for your own tasks in a channel, and why DMs differ.

Claude can use your own claude.ai connectors, called personal connectors, for your tasks in a Slack channel. See how you approve connector use, when Claude asks you to review a result before posting it, and what other people in the channel can reach.
How Claude Tag keeps credentials out of the sandbox, limits where a channel session's requests can go, and controls who can see artifacts and invoke Claude.

What Claude Tag stores on Anthropic's side, how long session transcripts and memory are kept, and what disconnecting a workspace, uninstalling the app, deleting a Slack channel, removing a scope, or leaving the organization does to that data.

Claude Tag settings map: the admin page for access and behavior, the usage page for spend limits, the in-Slack Configure link for channel instructions, and personal connectors for DMs and your own tasks in channels. Claude Managed Agents is configured separately on the Claude Platform.
Claude Tag for Claude Code users
Which parts of a Claude Code setup carry into Claude Tag, which move to admin settings, and how Slack threads map to sessions.
What the Claude Slack app can access
What the Claude app reads and posts in Slack, the OAuth scopes it requests, and what installing it does not grant. Written for the Slack admin approving the install.
Set up Claude Tag for your organization: pair your Slack workspace, add Claude to channels, launch, give Claude access to your tools, and check that it works.
Give Claude access to your tools
Add connectors so Claude Tag acts in your tools with its own credentials. Covers service accounts, bundles, allowed websites, domain entries, and plugins.
Give Claude its own GitHub identity through the Claude GitHub App. Covers linking your GitHub organization, granting repositories, and GitHub Actions.
Give Claude its own GitLab identity to read projects, manage issues, review merge requests, and check pipelines. Covers the account, token, and connector.
Claude Tag channel work bills to your organization's usage balance. Set the spend limit and see what happens when it's reached.
Set up Claude Tag for on-call
Put Claude on call for incident response in Slack: run setup at claude.ai/oncall, pick or auto-join incident channels, cap spend, and deploy.
Step-by-step setup for each tool Claude Tag can connect to. Each guide covers the dedicated account to create, the credential to enter, and the URL to allow.
Connect a service that isn't in the list
Connect a tool that isn't in Claude Tag's connector list. Covers credential types, what each form field means, and how to add a custom MCP server.
Connect Amplitude to Claude Tag with a project API key and secret key, or by signing in with Amplitude, so Claude can answer product-analytics questions.
Connect Asana to Claude Tag so it can file tasks and read project status. Covers the dedicated account to create, the token fields, and the URL to allow.
Connect Atlassian Cloud to Claude Tag so it can read and update Jira issues and search Confluence pages.
Connect BigQuery to Claude Tag so it can run read-only queries on your datasets, using a GCP service-account key.
Connect Datadog to Claude Tag so it can query metrics, logs, and monitors. Covers the dedicated account to create, the API key fields, and the URL to allow.

Connect GitLab to Claude Tag so it can read code, manage issues, comment on merge requests, and check pipelines through the GitLab API. Covers token permissions, self-managed hostnames, and how it differs from GitHub.
Connect Gong to Claude Tag so it can pull call summaries and deal context. Covers the dedicated account to create, the token fields, and the URL to allow.
Connect Google Drive, Calendar, and Gmail
Connect Google Drive, Calendar, and Gmail to Claude Tag so it can read docs, sheets, events, and email. Covers OAuth setup, the service-account option, and what each grants.
Connect HubSpot to Claude Tag so it can read pipeline, deal, and contact data. Covers the dedicated account to create, the token fields, and the URL to allow.
Connect Linear to Claude Tag so it can file tickets and post status updates. Covers the dedicated account to create, the token fields, and the URL to allow.
Connect Notion to Claude Tag so it can read and search your Notion workspace. Covers the dedicated account to create, the token fields, and the URL to allow.
Connect PagerDuty to Claude Tag so it can read incidents and on-call schedules. Covers the dedicated account to create, the token fields, and the URL to allow.
Connect Salesforce to Claude Tag so it can read and update CRM records. Covers the connected app to create, the client credential fields, and the host to allow.
Connect Sentry to Claude Tag so it can pull errors and stack traces into threads. Covers the dedicated account to create, the token fields, and the URL to allow.
Connect Snowflake to Claude Tag so it can run read-only queries on your warehouse. Covers the dedicated user to create, the access token field, and the host to allow.
Connect Stripe to Claude Tag so it can answer billing and subscription questions. Covers the dedicated account to create, the key fields, and the URL to allow.
Connect Vercel to Claude Tag so it can check deployment status and logs. Covers the dedicated account to create, the token fields, and the URL to allow.
Claude Tag proves its identity to your systems with a short-lived signed token instead of a credential stored in Claude. Learn how the token works and which of the four connection types to use.

Connect a gateway you run so Claude Tag can call your internal services with a short-lived identity token instead of a stored credential. Covers what the gateway must check, how to register it in the console, and how to verify the connection.

Let Claude sign in to an IAM role in your AWS account with a short-lived identity token instead of stored access keys. Covers the identity provider and trust policy to create in AWS, how to connect the role in the console, and how to verify the connection in CloudTrail.

Let Claude call Google Cloud through workload identity federation with a short-lived identity token instead of a service account key. Covers the pool, provider, and IAM grants to create, with or without a service account, and how to connect the identity in the console.

Let Claude exchange a short-lived identity token for an access token from an OAuth 2.0 authorization server you run, then call your APIs with it. Covers what your token endpoint receives and must check, what it returns, and how to register it in the console.
The claims, issuer, signing keys, lifetime, and subject format of the identity token Claude Tag presents to a gateway, cloud provider, or authorization server.
Counts, lengths, lifetimes, and unsupported configurations for Claude Tag's federated agent access: gateways, AWS roles, Google Cloud identities, and authorization servers.

Errors from Claude Tag's federated agent access and what fixes each: console dialog messages, requests Claude reports as blocked or failed, and rejections your gateway, AWS, Google Cloud, or authorization server records.
Choose which Slack workspaces and channels a Claude Tag bundle applies to, attach bundles to channels by name, and see how access stacks when bundles overlap.

Claude Tag responds only where it has been added and addressed. See who can invoke it, what changes in guest and Slack Connect channels, the per-scope version setting, how to limit it to chosen channels, how to delegate administration or a channel's setup, and how to quiet or remove it.
Connect more Slack workspaces or an Enterprise Grid to Claude Tag, choose which Claude Tag version each channel uses, and disconnect a workspace.
Use Claude Tag at a healthcare organization

Claude Tag is not covered by Anthropic's Business Associate Agreement. Configure it so protected health information never reaches a channel, direct message, or tool Claude can read: limit Claude to approved channels, turn off direct messages, and connect only PHI-free tools. Also covers what to do i…
Claude Tag is customized per channel and workspace (a scope), not per user. See what admins set in claude.ai, what anyone can change from the channel, and what stays fixed.
Manage a channel's instructions from another channel
Set up a skills repository Claude can update
Put your org's Claude Tag skills in a git repository with auto-sync, grant Claude write access, and Claude can open pull requests to improve its own skills from what it learns in channels.
Review what Claude Tag has done

Claude Tag actions appear under its own service accounts in each connected tool's audit log. See what the Activity page covers, how to trace an action to its source, and where each connected tool keeps logs.
Pull channel spend per Slack user from the Usage and Cost Analytics API for showback or chargeback reporting, and see how Claude's work is attributed to people.
Error messages from Claude Tag setup and what fixes each. Covers permission mismatches, GitHub access gaps, session start failures, and account errors.
Claude Tag reaches your services from a published egress range, over HTTP and HTTPS only. See the IP block to allowlist and how the allowlist relates to the allowed-websites setting on a connection.
Migrate from the earlier Claude in Slack
Claude Tag replaces the earlier per-user Claude in Slack app in place. See what changes, what stays, how to set the version, and what existing users notice.
Claude Tag works in your Slack channels. See how to check it's on, send your first message, what it can read, and why DMs work differently.

A few exact, bang-prefixed words after an @-mention run a fixed action instead of starting a normal turn: see the command list, get the link to a channel's settings page, restart a stuck or wrong-context session, check whether Claude is still working in a thread or channel, mute or unmute a thread,…
What Claude Tag does with a channel message nobody tagged it in, and how to turn unprompted replies off for a thread or a channel. Read this if Claude is replying too much, or went quiet.
Use Claude Tag in a group DM
Add Claude to a Slack group DM to share a task with a few people. See whose access and billing apply, when Claude replies, and what differs from a channel.
Good habits for working with Claude Tag
Name the outcome, give every task a definition of done, and pick the right channel. See how to write tasks Claude can finish and how to keep many threads reviewable.
Claude Tag runs routines you set up from a channel. See scheduled jobs, channel watching, pull request subscriptions, where results post, and how to pause them.
Claude Tag memory belongs to the channel, not to you. See what each channel keeps, which notes are shared across the workspace, and how to check or correct them.
Choose the model Claude Tag uses

Ask Claude to switch models in a Slack thread, set a channel's default model, pick the model for your direct messages, or run a thread in fast mode. See which models you can use and how to confirm which one replied.
Copy-paste prompts for Claude Tag in Slack, each with why it works. See first messages, handoffs, channel rules, memory checks, routines, fan-out, and steering.
Troubleshoot Claude Tag in channels and DMs
Fixes for common Claude Tag problems in Slack. See no reply after a reaction, queued or failed sessions, lost work, missing connections, blocked links and websites, and DM or account errors.
Shapes of work teams hand Claude Tag in Slack, each with prompts to paste. See triage, catch-up, docs and tickets, project tracking, data, deals, monitoring, and bug fixes.

Claude Tag triages a Slack request channel with two setup messages. See in-thread answers, duplicate flags, owner routing, weekly theme rollups, optional ticket filing, and runbooks of standing answers.
Claude Tag summarizes Slack threads and channels on demand. See one-off recaps, a scheduled morning rollup of open threads, and what's waiting on you.

Create a Slack channel for you and Claude Tag alone and run your work from it. See scratch questions, digests of channels you don't follow, a weekly status digest, follow-ups chased until they close, and a handoff that covers your time away.
Turn threads into docs and tickets

Claude Tag turns a Slack discussion into the artifact you name. See replies you can send, decision docs, status memos, filed tickets, hosted web pages, page comments that reach Claude, and a capture-channel pattern.
Claude Tag posts project digests no one has to compile. See standing status updates and follow-ups on contracts, design reviews, and pull requests until they close.
Claude Tag answers data questions in the Slack thread. See warehouse queries with charts, scheduled metric reports, and charts built from channel history alone.
Claude Tag finds answers in connected docs and replies in the thread. See policy lookups, runbook checks, prior decisions, and answers from the Slack channel alone.

Claude Tag reviews documents in a connected tool against a checklist or policy and posts findings in the thread. See single-document checks, batch reviews, filing lists, comparisons with past reviews, and a scheduled weekly sweep.
Claude Tag pulls account and deal state into the Slack channel. See in-thread account answers, pre-call briefs, and a scheduled weekly pipeline digest.

Claude Tag recipes for marketing teams in Slack. See policy answers in an intake channel, campaign channel recaps and send-ready drafts, lead and campaign state from the CRM, a weekly metrics digest, and brand voice rules saved to channel memory.
Claude Tag watches dashboards and alert channels so you see one line per issue. See scheduled checks, alert investigation before anyone asks, and the prompts to set both up.
Claude Tag takes a bug report from Slack to a draft pull request. See reproducing the issue, watching a bug channel, root-cause digs, and following CI to green.
Claude Tag works with your GitHub repositories from Slack: answer questions in-thread, subscribe to pull requests, and hand back chores as draft pull requests.

provenance.basis: Human0's claude_domain.csv (sha256 d26d41d8da4ed7dd622b6e6faa18a97dc91d4f3d2af972ae9715d41ee94963cc), converted by tools/claude_domain/build_claude_packs.py on 2026-11-27. Topics, concepts, skills (docs pages) and agent names are Human0's. A single-page skill's description is that page's own one-line description where the site publishes one (page_descriptions.json: llms.txt / llms-full.txt fetched 2026-11-27); concept descriptions, other skill descriptions, keywords, skill types (a verb rule), ids and the lexicon are generated from the CSV text.
provenance.mcp_notes: Human0's CSV lists 'Claude Developer Platform docs' for this topic, but that server (Claude Platform Docs, directory cc6f3470-080c-45b8-84e1-cdc03e9c6ac1) covers platform.claude.com only, by its own instructions, and a search for 'Claude Code hooks' on 2026-11-27 returned only platform.claude.com pages. No MCP server for these docs was verified, so the pack lists none.
provenance.limitations: Skills without a published page description (API reference endpoints and some guides) are described by their titles only; skill types come from the first word of the title. Docs pages change: the URLs were current in the CSV, not re-checked here.
